name: Yemen
summary: A plain horizontal tricolour of red, white and black, in the Pan-Arab colours. It was adopted on 22 May 1990, when North and South Yemen united.
origin: North Yemen used red-white-black with a green star from 1962, and South Yemen used red-white-black with a blue triangle and red star from 1967. At unification, the emblems were dropped, leaving the plain tricolour.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of martyrs and unity.

history.label: People's Democratic Republic (South)
history.note: Blue triangle with a red star.

facts: Egypt, Iraq and Syria use the same colours with added emblems; Yemen's has none.
Southern separatists still use the former flag of South Yemen.
It is the simplest of the red-white-black Pan-Arab flags.
clues: Plain red, white and black horizontal bands.
Adopted when two states united in 1990.
Egypt's and Iraq's flags are similar but add emblems.
